name: Norfloxacin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Norfloxacin is a fluoroquinolone excreted largely unchanged in urine (33% to 48% in 24 hours); its half-life rises from 3–4 hours to about 8 hours at creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. The New Zealand data sheet halves the daily dose to 400 mg once daily at CrCl below 30 (not on hemodialysis) and has no data for gonorrhea in that group. Fluoroquinolone class warnings apply. It has no current US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: New Zealand data sheet uses creatinine clearance indexed to body surface area (CrCl, mL/min/1.73 m2); threshold 30.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 400 mg twice daily (urinary tract infection 7 to 10 days; gastroenteritis 5 days; chronic prostatitis 3 to 7 weeks); maximum 800 mg/day (data sheet).
No dose change at CrCl ≥30 (data sheet).
CrCl <30 (not on hemodialysis): 400 mg once daily. No dose recommendation for gonorrhea at CrCl ≤30 (data sheet).
400 mg once daily; half-life about 8 hours, the same at CrCl <10 and 10–30 (data sheet). Low urinary levels may limit efficacy in urinary infections (our caution).

hd: The data sheet's reduced dose excludes patients on hemodialysis; no hemodialysis dosing is given. Specialist input; consider another agent.
pd: No PD dosing in the data sheet.
crrt: No data; oral agent rarely used in CRRT settings.
monitoring: Tendinopathy (higher risk with kidney impairment, transplant, corticosteroids, age); QT risk factors; glucose with sulfonylureas or insulin (dysglycemia, hypoglycemic coma); seizures; hydration (crystalluria). Separate from iron, zinc, antacids, sucralfate by 2 hours (data sheet).

pediatric.approved_ages: Contraindicated in pre-pubertal children; not for growing adolescents (data sheet).
